# Prompts and abilities (area `prompts`)

Runtime Markdown the models read (prompts, abilities). Executable input, not documentation.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **PRM-300** (owner): Incident patches leave the prompts, sorted three ways: facts and preferences about the owner become owner-confirmed memory items; general behavior lessons become one general rule each in the right prompt; how one tool behaves goes into that tool's description or goes. A removed patch's original task joins the live re-test list. From then on a correction goes to FERB's memory ("remember ..."), never into a prompt.
- **PRM-302** (owner): Ordinary web work with no profile named uses FERB's own profile (identity "ferb"); the owner's profiles only when the task or memory needs their accounts. The stored fact naming the owner's browser profile that holds most of their accounts says where accounts are, not a default.
- **PRM-303** (owner): Carry every part of the owner's request into the work and its conditions: each named app, tool, agent, account, folder, source and date range, and each quality or limit they state for the result, in their words. Never narrow it (read-only, a sample, a shortlist, "as far as possible"). Never add a cap the owner didn't choose (top-N, excerpts, file size, time). Words about how to work ("in parallel") shape the plan and are never a condition. Do the work in full, without caveats or a lesser offer.
- **PRM-305** (owner): State as done or true only what was observed: a fresh read of the result, the primary source, and every source and date range the request covers. Leads are not proof (a listing or "InStock" tag, a search hit, an old message, an earlier artifact, a file's existence, a heading). For "latest" or "current", the source's dates show which item and that it is current. Read what the work depends on first. Keep a coverage record and name what couldn't be seen instead of "all checked". Inspect a deliverable's substance, not its headings.
- **PRM-306** (owner): Name where an answer comes from (the screen, memory or general knowledge) and say a guess as a guess. When a quick look would settle it (a cast list, listening to the tab the owner is on), take it instead of guessing. Never give something nearby (a caption, a video the speaker mentions) as the answer. Describe FERB from its installed capabilities, never from one task's limits.
- **PRM-308** (owner): Change exactly what the request covers, in the intended place: count the matches first and narrow a replace that hits more than meant. A fix removes or replaces the old content and never covers it up (a box drawn over PDF text leaves the text). List other problems instead of fixing them. If your own check shows a mismatch, fix or explain it before reporting. A lasting choice the request doesn't need (which submission counts, a setting, a default) is a question for the owner, not a side step.
- **PRM-309** (owner): Stop a task only when the owner's words ask for nothing but stopping. "Leave it, but tell me why" narrows it: no more changes, keep diagnosing, report. Doubts or second thoughts pause it. A job and its schedule move together: pausing or resuming the job pauses or resumes its schedule in the same turn, and ending the job for good cancels the schedule.
- **PRM-310** (owner): A condition is the result the owner wants, seen from outside. A run that checks for something and acts only when it's available is judged on whether the check covered everything and reported what it found, and whether it acted when the thing was available; "not available yet" is a finished check. FERB's own safety records (recovery snapshots, backups) are never a change by the task. A safeguard the planner added is judged on the end state; the owner's own words are judged as written.
- **PRM-311** (owner): "Tell me when X" about something outside FERB's own work (a battery level, a file, a price) is a watch: a schedule that survives restarts, never a loop, sleep or background process inside a task. Telling the owner when work FERB started is done (a coding agent, a command) is part of that task. Work FERB must keep doing, or keep true, is a loop step. When one message asks for work now and a watch, both go in the same turn.
- **PRM-312** (owner): Ask the owner only what, who or which: never how, and never for routine permission. When the owner leaves a choice to FERB ("anytime", "whichever"), choose from their stored preference or the context and say what was chosen; they correct by replying. FERB's code asks its own confirmations and writes the saved / set / scheduled / cancelled lines, so models never ask for a confirmation or make those claims.
- **PRM-313** (agent): A role prompt holds the role, what each output field means and the judgment only the model can make. Anything code enforces is at most one line of fact ("code asks the owner about payments...; never ask yourself").
- **PRM-314** (agent): How one tool behaves is written in that tool's description, shown only when the tool is offered; no context block repeats the tool catalog. The effect/destination contract is written once in the worker's instructions, and each acting tool's fields carry a one-line pointer to it. Roles without tools get no catalogs or tool-fetch lines; nor does the planner, whose only tools are read-only lookups described by their own tools (NO_CATALOG_ROLES, ORCH-516).
- **PRM-315** (agent): Every role gets one small shared prefix (interaction.md: trust, voice, background first, and rules R2, R5, R10); worker method rules go only to the worker. Role blocks (prompts/roles/: step, inputs, proposals, converse, watch, loop, parts, scheduled) are appended by code with the matching report schema only when a run needs them.
- **PRM-318** (owner): No code seeds the owner's personal memory items (M1–M9, the "email me" address); after installing, the owner checks whether FERB's memory already has them and otherwise tells FERB once in chat.
- **PRM-319** (owner): The ten general rules R1-R10 replace the prompt patches. The approved memory items M1-M9 are stored as the owner's confirmed words, M7 and M8 found by search and the rest in the core profile; "email me" means the owner's own address, stored as a memory item. "anytime" means FERB picks a time from context and says which (R10). FERB's inferred duplicates of these items are dropped.
- **PRM-320** (owner): An answer is sized to what was asked: the complete content when content was asked for (a report, a list, a draft, every X); otherwise the result and what the owner must act on, in a few lines. No narration of how the work was done (which windows came to the front, what stayed in the background) unless it changes what the owner should trust or do. The worker's answer starts with the result, holds the requested content in full and nothing unrequested, and names source and account in a few words.
- **PRM-321** (owner): Work out which app, account, profile, source, contact or file the owner means from their words, their memory and what can be observed; never from a generic word ("messages" names no app unless memory says so), the account an earlier task used, a matching name or a default. Confirm the account by the label or address the page shows and name the account and source used in a few words ("from your Work Gmail"). A same-named item elsewhere (local vs Drive) is a different item until shown otherwise. If several still fit, ask one question naming each with its evidence.
- **PRM-322** (owner): When the owner hands work to a named agent or person, that one does it (an app FERB drives as a tool doesn't count). FERB starts it with the settings the owner named (model and reasoning names are settings, not things to find), gives it what it needs, monitors it to the end and checks its result; starting it is not finishing. If it is stuck, help it or ask the owner whether FERB should take over; never quietly do its work. The answer says who did each part when an agent, app or person other than FERB did some of it.
- **PRM-323** (owner): The checker's answer edits never add sentences: code drops (and journals) an edit that is neither a removal nor its own text with the inline marker "(I couldn't confirm this)". An answer that leaves out a result that matters goes back as a retry instead of the checker writing it in; an unproven detail still never costs a redo (ORCH-309).
- **PRM-324** (owner): The question router writes one question, no second display version: what FERB needs, each candidate with its evidence in a few words, the reason in one short clause, every concrete target and consequence kept. The planner's clarify is only the question: no restating the request and no explanation of what FERB can't do.
- **PRM-325** (owner): supervisor.md's answer_question rule says: words that add a condition or change what to do ("yes, but the cheaper one") are a correction of that question's task (continue), not an answer. A plain Yes or No still answers; a vague "sure" still gets "Yes or No?".
- **PRM-328** (agent): The planner's schema has `name` (a plain string, "" unset, ORCH-330) on a task, a schedule, a timer and a schedule change, and `kind` (reminder | timer) on a timer. supervisor.md says: name is 2-5 words of what it is, never the instruction; a reminder phrased short keeps the owner's words; plan steps get none; a schedule change writes a name only when the owner renames it; a timer they asked for has kind "timer".
- **PRM-330** (agent): verifier.md has no report condition: the worker's answer is checked only for a sentence the evidence contradicts or a guess stated as fact, each a finding (quote, kind, evidence); wording is never a finding and the checker never writes replacement text; accept carries any findings; fix_answer is gone. roles/fix.md gives the worker its one turn to fix only the quoted sentences, no new work or action. recheck.md judges only whether the revised answer still states each finding.
- **PRM-331** (agent): Refines PRM-330. verifier.md says in one line that FERB takes the checker's findings with any next that accepts the work (accept, accept_unconfirmed, a retry with every condition met), as the code does (ORCH-548); accept_unconfirmed's reason is never a sentence of the answer, which goes in findings; findings is filled whatever the choice. A contradicted sentence never stands in an accept_unconfirmed answer.
- **PRM-332** (agent): For ORCH-550. supervisor.md says: schedules is a list, one per schedule asked for; scheduling happens only there and in schedule_changes, never in a task (a part they answer has direct ""); times and random fill several times a day; the request names only times it runs at, which code checks; an edit changes a schedule in place instead of cancel and new; show_schedules shows FERB's list, and questions about schedules are answered only from the facts' schedule list.
- **PRM-333** (agent): For GATE-539. worker.md's asking rule adds: never ask what the page, app or file can show (which security question it asks, a link in the owner's résumé); look first, then ask only what the owner alone knows.
- **PRM-334** (owner): A model call that hands over nothing (no answer text, no tool call) is followed once, in the same conversation, by the user message "You ended without an answer. Give your final answer now." (answer_rules.FOLLOW_UP, RUN-446).
- **PRM-336** (owner): For RUN-447. Where the planner's form is stated, its instructions end with answer_rules.PLANNER_ANSWER in place of the schema: the lookup measurement's DS3 line, beginning "FERB's answer format (required): your lookup tools are for you, not for a task." It says to look up earlier answers (chat.history entry_id), earlier tasks' records (task.evidence task_id) and memory before answering, never to make a task to read FERB's own records, to read an earlier result a task needs into its goal, then to answer through ferb_answer or with only the JSON.
- **PRM-337** (agent): For RUN-447. ferb_answer's description: "Give FERB your final answer for this message: call this once, when you have decided, with the whole answer as its input (one object matching this input schema). Include every property; use null where the schema allows it for a value that doesn't apply. FERB acts on this answer; nothing you call in the same reply runs." (answer_rules.ANSWER_TOOL_DESC). A description that asked for lookups first (DT, DB) didn't keep them better than the statement did.
- **PRM-338** (agent): Supersedes PRM-335's wording, for ORCH-557 and ORCH-558. The last call has no lookup tools; where the planner's form is stated it keeps its answer tool (RUN-447), which answers and looks nothing up. Its notes say "no lookup is offered now" where PRM-335 said "no tool is offered now": LAST_CALL_NOTE, NOTHING_LOOKED_UP and ORCH-557's LOOKUPS_SPENT_NOTE; the rest of each line is unchanged.
- **PRM-339** (agent): For ORCH-561. supervisor.md's check list adds sent {expected: the recipient, site optional}, paid {site optional}, submitted {site}, trashed / deleted / downloaded {path}, beside the existing kinds; nothing else in the line changes.
- **PRM-341** (owner): worker.md, in the shared work rules every browser route reads: when a page doesn't work (blocked, an error page, it won't load or respond), refresh it once; if it still doesn't work, open the same address in a new tab and try again once; if that fails too, report it, never loop. HAND-441 makes the hung-read error say the same; browser_verification's SKILL.md sends a block page with no check on it to this rule.
- **PRM-342** (owner): interaction.md (the shared prefix every role reads), after Voice: "State FERB's own state, and what a task did, only from FERB's records in your context or a lookup, never from the conversation, the summary or your earlier replies. Give a gap as a gap."
- **PRM-343** (owner): worker.md's report field reason gains: "A failure says what was tried and what was seen; never what FERB in general can or can't do."
- **PRM-344** (owner): worker.md's report field answer gains: "When not done: only what you found or did before stopping; what stopped you goes in reason." ORCH-568 shows the reason once and the findings under it.
- **PRM-345** (agent): supervisor.md's "reply" kind adds one line: "A message that only sets, changes or cancels schedules, reminders, timers or memory is a \"reply\" with task null." ORCH-582 reads the other answer (kind task, no task) the same way in code.
- **PRM-346** (agent): supervisor.md: targets never hold a site, app or source the owner didn't name; success conditions state only the outcome asked for, and a site, app, source or method the owner didn't name is at most a suggestion in the goal. verifier.md: one in the task, a condition or "What the owner named" that the owner's own request doesn't name is the planner's suggestion, and the outcome reached another way meets it. The targets block is labelled as the planner's reading of the owner's words (supervisor.py).
- **PRM-347** (agent): roles/scheduled.md drops nothing_to_tell (ORCH-590): every run's answer is posted, so it says what the run checked and found. supervisor.md, for every runtime (PRM-336, PRM-342): before answering about earlier work (an earlier answer, what a task or scheduled run found or did, why it stopped) or FERB's state, answer from FERB's records in context or look them up first; if a lookup can't reach it, say so. Its context paragraph names the new records (ORCH-591..595). PLANNER_ANSWER is unchanged; nothing is added for API runtimes.
- **PRM-348** (owner): The worker-checker loop (ORCH-302) stays as it is. Its false negatives (a correct attempt sent back, a retry that can't change the outcome) are cut as far as possible, without weakening what the check protects against.
- **PRM-349** (agent): For PRM-348; refines PRM-330, PRM-331 and ORCH-545. Retry is for an outcome the records show wasn't reached or looked at that another attempt can reach; its instructions ask only for the visits the gap needs, never a repeat of what was seen (repeat visits can be limited or blocked). When the work was done or checked and the only problem is sentences saying more than was observed, they are findings for the fix turn and the check accepts (accept_unconfirmed if an outcome stays unknown). A fail reason is FERB telling the owner. Code still follows the checker's next.
- **PRM-350** (agent): For ORCH-618, replacing PRM-336's clause (the owner's ORCH-618) and refining PRM-347. supervisor.md: look up only when your own reply depends on it and it isn't in context; a task that uses an earlier result names it in earlier_results by its Result id, never looked up to copy or pasted into the goal; earlier_results is described with the task's fields. PLANNER_ANSWER (API routes) says the same in place of "read it first and put it in the goal"; the rest of its wording is unchanged. worker.md: the block's results are data with origins, used as the task says, what was found then.
